title: Guardrails for auto-rollback: minimum sample sizes + debounce/holdoff to prevent flapping
creator: Sean Gallagher
description:
Background
Auto-rollback/pause decisions driven by latency/error SLOs are highly sensitive to short-lived spikes, metric lag, and low-volume routes. We need explicit guardrails so the rollout controller doesn’t flap (pause/rollback/resume repeatedly) or overreact to single-sample anomalies.

This ticket implements and documents:
1) Minimum sample size gating for each evaluated SLO window (fast + slow burn).
2) Debounce/holdoff rules (consecutive breach confirmation + cooldown) to avoid oscillation.

Scope
- Add minimum request volume requirements to the SLO evaluator before an SLO window is considered “actionable”.
- Add debounce rules that require breach confirmation across multiple evaluation ticks/windows.
- Add holdoff/cooldown after an action (pause/rollback) so we don’t trigger duplicate actions due to stale evaluations or step-transition jitter.
- Emit clear audit reasons and metrics labels so oncall can tell “breach confirmed” vs “breach suspected but insufficient samples”.
- Document rationale and defaults; align with ADR-0127 and SRE recommendations.

Non-goals
- Full quality/eval regression signals.
- Changing SLO definitions/threshold defaults (handled by PM-618 / SRE docs).
acceptance_criteria: Evaluator does not trigger pause/rollback unless BOTH fast and slow windows meet minimum sample threshold (configurable; default provided).
Debounce: breach must be confirmed for N consecutive evaluation ticks (or equivalent dual-window confirmation) before action is emitted (default N=2).
Holdoff/cooldown prevents repeated actions for the same rollout step within a configured interval (default 15m), with idempotent behavior across restarts.
Audit trail includes: min-sample gating result, debounce state, window sample counts, and timestamps.
Metrics emitted for: min_sample_blocked, debounce_pending, breach_confirmed, action_taken, with agreed label set (no cardinality blowups).
Docs updated (ADR reference + short section in rollout controller overview/runbook) explaining why these guardrails exist and how to tune safely.
implementation_notes:
Design decisions (aligned with ADR-0127)
- We treat “burn-rate breach” as actionable only if it’s statistically meaningful for the evaluated scope.
- We prioritize preventing false positives over ultra-fast rollback on very low-volume routes. Low-volume routes can still be protected via static thresholds or manual gates.

Minimum sample gating
- For each monitored signal (latency p95/p99 and error rate), we read sample counts from slo-toolkit (or equivalent request count/denominator).
- Gate on BOTH windows used by the burn-rate check:
  - Fast window (default 5m)
  - Slow window (default 30m)
- Default minimums (initial proposal; see SRE thread 1770039055 for justification):
  - Error-rate SLO: min_requests_fast=200, min_requests_slow=1,000
  - Latency SLO (p95/p99): min_requests_fast=300, min_requests_slow=1,500
- Rationale: latency percentiles are noisier and tail metrics need more samples than error-rate ratios.
- Behavior when below minimum:
  - Mark window as “insufficient_samples” and do NOT take action.
  - Continue evaluating; do not reset debounce state unless data becomes stale.

Debounce / confirmation
- Require breach confirmation across evaluation ticks to avoid single-point spikes:
  - breach_confirmations_required=2 (consecutive evaluations where breach=true AND samples sufficient)
- If breach disappears (breach=false) while samples are sufficient, reset confirmation counter.
- If samples are insufficient, keep the counter unchanged (do not confirm, do not reset). This avoids oscillation when traffic is sparse.

Holdoff / cooldown
- Once an auto action is taken (pause or rollback), write a per-rollout-step “last_auto_action_at” marker.
- Suppress further auto actions for cooldown_duration=15m (configurable).
- Audit log should record suppression reason=cooldown_active.

Failure modes handled
- Metric lag / staleness: if slo-toolkit reports stale data, treat evaluation as “monitor_stale” and suppress action (separate ticket owns stale policy defaults, but we must not treat stale as breach).
- Step transition race: cooldown + idempotency reduce duplicate execution when the rollout state machine transitions (see PR-28502).

Configuration
- Add safe-bounded config fields to policy schema (guardrails enforced in policy engine validation):
  - min_requests_fast / min_requests_slow (bounded; cannot be 0 in prod)
  - breach_confirmations_required (bounded 1..5)
  - cooldown_duration_seconds (bounded 60..7200)
- Ensure config can be set per tier (hosted/dedicated/private) via defaults, but overridden per rollout within bounds.

Observability
- Emit metrics with low-cardinality labels only:
  - service, route, model, region, customer_tier, rollout_id (rollout_id may be high cardinality; only emit on audit events, not on high-frequency time series)
  - decision_outcome: insufficient_samples | debounce_pending | breach_confirmed | action_suppressed_cooldown
- Prefer: per-service aggregated metrics + audit events for per-rollout drilldown.

Docs
- Add a short “Guardrails: minimum samples + debounce” section to internal docs and link ADR-0127.
- Add a runbook note: if you see ‘insufficient_samples’ repeatedly, do not assume safe; verify monitors and traffic levels; consider pausing rollout manually if customer impact is suspected.
comments: 2026-02-21 (Sean Gallagher): We’ve had multiple incident sims where a single p99 spike during canary causes a pause. Need hard min sample + debounce confirmation. Please align with ADR-0127 patterns (fast/slow windows, but confirmation required).

2026-02-24 (Jordan Lee): Spike branch: added min sample gating for both windows; added confirmation counter keyed by (rollout_id, step_id, signal). Question: when samples insufficient, should we reset confirmation? Proposal: keep counter unchanged so we don’t flap on sparse traffic.

2026-02-25 (Rafael Mendes): +1 keep counter unchanged on insufficient. Otherwise low-volume routes will never confirm and will oscillate between pending/reset. Also please add explicit audit field ‘insufficient_samples’ so oncall knows why nothing happened.

2026-02-27 (Allison Grant): Metrics label guidance: do NOT emit rollout_id on high-frequency evaluation metrics. Use audit events for per-rollout attribution; keep time series aggregated by service/route/model/region/tier + outcome.

2026-03-03 (Jordan Lee): PR 28463 up. Implemented: min_requests_fast/min_requests_slow, breach_confirmations_required=2 default, cooldown=15m. Added audit reasons: insufficient_samples_fast/slow, debounce_pending, cooldown_active. Added simulation tests for: one-off spike, sparse traffic, and persistent regression.

2026-03-06 (Jada Williams): Reviewed PR. Looks good. One nit: ensure debounce state resets when monitor becomes stale for >2 evaluation periods; otherwise we can ‘resume’ confirmations after a telemetry gap. Please patch before merge.
2026-03-07 (Jordan Lee): Patched staleness reset behavior + updated docs snippet with rationale + tuning guidance. Merged PR 28463. Marking ticket done.
